--- title: "Calibration limits (4.1–4.3)" --- ::: {.cell} ::: Page 4 of the app, **Calibration and quantification**, turns the signals of the targeted compounds into concentrations. At the top you choose the **normalization method** (the best one, Multivariate (PCA), is preselected) and the **batch**; the tables and figures follow. The examples below show batch 1. How a calibration curve is made, in short: 1. The **zero calibrant** (`Cal0`) gives two signal thresholds: 3× and 10× its mean signal (or its mean plus 3 and 10 standard deviations). 2. The **LOD** is the lowest calibration level whose mean signal is above the first threshold, the **LLOQ** the lowest above the second (and, with the RSD% option, with an RSD% of at most 20%). 3. The curve is fitted from the LLOQ upwards: linear or quadratic, weighted 1, 1/x or 1/x², the combination with the highest R². 4. The **ULOQ** is the top of the curve's linear range (see 4.2 and the next chapter). ## 4.1 Calibration curve samples ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: The number of calibration samples per concentration level in the chosen batch: the replicates the curve of this batch is fitted on. ## 4.2 Calibration curve limits ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: One row per targeted compound with its limits in the chosen batch. In the app, **select a row** (or step with the arrow keys ↑ / ↓) to show that compound in figures 4.4–4.6. **How to read it** - **Calibration**: the curve used for the compound in this batch: the batch's own (*Batch*), the curve of all batches together (*Global*, blue rows), or none (red rows). - **LOD and LLOQ** are calibration levels; values below them are replaced or reported as *n.d.* / *n.q.* (see 4.5). - **Highest cal. conc.** is the highest level the curve is fitted on; the **ULOQ** is the top of its linear range. They differ when the top levels bend away from the line and the curve was not cut there (option *Enforce linear range*), or was cut but keeps the minimum number of calibration levels. A quadratic curve has no ULOQ. - **Notes** show an icon per kind of note; **hover an icon** for the full text: - **No valid curve**: No valid curve: e.g. too few levels above the LLOQ, no signal, or R² below the minimum. The row is red. - **Kept although not valid**: Kept although not valid (option *Keep all calibration curves*). The row is orange. - **Global curve used**: The batch's own curve is not valid, or the batch has too few replicates: the global curve is used. - **Linear range (ULOQ)**: Linear range: levels above the ULOQ, which were cut off or are above the linear range. - **Detection in samples**: Detection in the samples: not detected in any study sample, or detected but below the LLOQ (not exported). - **Removed before calibration**: Removed before calibration by the blank filter or the QC RSD% filter. The row is grey. The exported tables have the same notes in full, as text. ## 4.3 Chemicals with concentrations ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: The number of compounds per batch with a valid calibration curve **and** concentrations in the samples. Compounds without any study sample at or above the LLOQ are not quantified and not exported.
